AI slop just booked a one-way trip to Portugal

Lisbon streets, ocean views, Lacoste fits and a sunset dance in 30 seconds

Seedance 2.5 on Dreamina_ai 

Prompt ↓

[GENERATION GOAL]
30-second photoreal cinematic fashion-travel music video of a beautiful sweet slim young woman spending one energetic day in Portugal — Lisbon tram streets, tiled courtyards, ocean cliffs and a sunset coastal plaza. She listens to music through white wired earphones, carries a small Canon compact camera, wears Lacoste throughout three changing fashion looks, and ends dancing with a friend. Hard cuts only. No fades. No slow motion except one brief hair movement.

[LEAD]
Generate an original beautiful sweet slim woman in her early 20s. Delicate oval face, large dark-brown eyes, long straight black hair, soft winged eyeliner, long lashes, glossy peach-nude lips, warm light skin, slim athletic figure, elegant hands, long nude manicured nails, tiny silver earrings. Naturally beautiful, sweet expression, subtle smile becoming genuine laughter. No glasses. She never speaks.

White wired earphones remain in both ears whenever she appears, with cable clearly visible.

[FRIEND]
Appears only from 22 seconds. Young Portuguese woman, early 20s, long chestnut hair, soft round face, loose pale-blue shirt, cream trousers and white sneakers. No earphones.

[FASHION / PRODUCTS]
LOOK A 0–7s:
Lacoste crimson zip track jacket, white fitted top, black trousers, white sneakers, small black shoulder bag, Canon compact camera.

LOOK B 7–17s:
Lacoste forest-green cropped polo jacket, cream wide-leg trousers, thin gold chain, stacked bracelets, small cream handbag.

LOOK C 17–30s:
Lacoste black lightweight jacket with subtle white detailing, charcoal cargo pants, silver belt, white sneakers.

No Adidas, Puma or Nike. Lacoste crocodile branding remains physically correct and minimal. Canon camera stays consistent.

[LOCATIONS]
LOC 1 — Lisbon hillside street:
Yellow tram tracks, pastel buildings, balconies with plants, patterned stone pavement, bright Atlantic sky.

LOC 2 — Blue-tile courtyard:
Historic tiled walls, stone fountain, flowering plants and natural tourists.

LOC 3 — Narrow staircase:
Long stone steps between colorful buildings, tourists moving naturally.

LOC 4 — Pastry shop:
Close-up of a custard tart being placed on a ceramic plate.

LOC 5 — Tram interior:
Vintage yellow tram, wooden seats, sunlight flickering through windows.

LOC 6 — Ocean cliff:
Dark rocky edge, powerful Atlantic waves, green grass.

LOC 7 — Coastal road:
White stone walls, eucalyptus trees and distant ocean.

LOC 8 — Lighthouse:
White lighthouse above rugged coastline, hazy horizon.

LOC 9 — Fishing harbor:
Small colorful boats, ropes, wet stone quay.

LOC 10 — Sunset plaza:
Open stone square overlooking ocean, warm lamps and pastel buildings.

[TIMELINE]

0–2.5s
35mm handheld. Lead walks downhill through Lisbon street in LOOK A, camera following backward. She checks Canon camera, earphone cable bouncing naturally.

2.5–4.2s
85mm ECU. Her nude nails adjust camera lens and press shutter.

4.2–7s
50mm portrait beside tiled wall. She raises camera, lowers it and gives a tiny sweet smile. Sun catches her cheek.

7–9s
Hard cut on her smile. LOOK B. She steps onto stone staircase, turning her head toward camera.

9–11.2s
24mm low-angle staircase shot. She climbs through tourists while holding cream handbag.

11.2–13s
Close pastry insert. Custard tart lands on ceramic plate, tiny crumbs moving.

13–15s
35mm tram interior. She sits beside window, earphones visible, watching Lisbon pass.

15–17s
50mm reflection in tram glass. Her eyes meet camera reflection and she smiles.

17–19.2s
Hard cut to ocean cliff. LOOK C. She walks toward railing, wind moving black jacket.

19.2–21s
24mm wide. She reaches cliff edge and looks toward Atlantic waves.

21–22.4s
85mm portrait. Hair moves across her cheek. She laughs softly.

22.4–24.5s
Friend enters at harbor. Lead turns and immediately smiles.

24.5–26.5s
35mm tracking. Both walk beside fishing boats, comparing the Canon camera photos and laughing.

26.5–28s
Low-angle shot. They run a few steps toward sunset plaza.

28–30s
Wide-to-medium dance. Both casually dance on stone plaza overlooking ocean.
At 28.4s giant mustard-yellow condensed type:
【PORTUGAL】
At 29.1s it changes to:
【LIVE A LITTLE】
Final frame: lead laughing with one arm raised.
Hard cut to black.

[CAMERA]
35mm movement, 50mm portraits, 85mm details, 24mm landscapes. Handheld walking energy, gentle lateral tracking and one natural spin. No drone orbit, no crash zooms.

[PHYSICS]
Real hair weight, natural jacket wrinkles, realistic earphone cable movement, authentic ocean wind, natural pedestrian motion, believable camera weight and reflections.

[AUDIO]
Tram bell, footsteps, camera shutter, distant café ambience, ocean wind, waves, harbor ropes, natural laughter. No dialogue or voiceover. Only specified English title cards.

[CONSISTENCY]
One original lead throughout. Friend only after 22s. White wired earphones always visible. Lacoste fashion only. Canon compact camera consistent. Photoreal live action.

The future of fashion is kind. 💚✨ 

PETA India, as the supporting partner of ET Retail's ShopFWD Summit 2026, spotlighted innovative vegan fashion brands and next-generation materials that prove style never has to come at the cost of an animal's life. 

At our stall, visitors explored a wide range of cruelty-free alternatives, discovering how conscious material choices can benefit animals, humans, and the planet. Our showcase featured pioneering vegan brands and materials that are helping reshape the future of fashion, while a powerful video featuring Karishma Tanna highlighted the suffering animals endure for leather, wool, exotic skins, and other animal-derived materials. 

A key highlight of the event was Jeev, PETA India’s AI-powered robo calf, who engaged attendees in meaningful one-on-one conversations about the realities of the fashion industry and inspired them to consider kinder, animal-free alternatives. 

Adding to the dialogue, Ashima Kukreja, PETA India’s Director of Corporate Affairs, joined a panel discussion on how material innovation, responsible sourcing, brand accountability, and evolving consumer values are driving the fashion industry's next chapter. 

As consumer demand for ethical and sustainable products continues to grow, events like these demonstrate that innovation and compassion can go hand in hand. The future of fashion is what not only reflects style but also responsibility and kindness.

This paper points out something that should have been obvious to all of us.

We’ve spent the last 2 years throwing massive diffusion models at offline RL actors just to handle multimodal data, and just pretending that a 50ms denoising loop per step is fine for robotics. 

The reality is it isn’t.

The argument of this paper is dead simple: the critic gets thrown away the second training ends. 

The actor is the only thing that actually has to run live on hardware. 

So why on earth are we stuffing all the compute into the actor?

People avoided deep critics before because offline value networks love to diverge into oblivion, but they managed to stabilize a deep residual critic using n-step targets and categorical cross-entropy. 

That lets the critic do the heavy lifting during training, so runtime is left to a tiny deterministic policy that runs in a single forward pass. 

It matches diffusion performance on OGBench while running 4x faster, no distillation hacks needed.

And i feel its genuinely a great work and definitely worth a read.

Read the full paper here: https://t.co/i0FVJuJUR2

Abraham Wald wrote eight memoranda at Columbia in 1943 about which parts of a bomber to armor and did not draw a single plane. The Center for Naval Analyses printed all eight as a monograph in July 1980.

The Statistical Research Group he wrote them inside had Milton Friedman, George Stigler, Jacob Wolfowitz, and a bench of thirty Hunter and Vassar women running the numbers. Two future Nobel laureates sat at the same table counting bullet holes on planes that came home.

Wald wrote out the calculation and told the Navy to armor the parts of the returning bombers that had no bullet holes.

The image every teacher points at, a bomber silhouette dotted in red where the fire went, is not in the memoranda. Somebody else drew it later and gave it his name. The mathematics is what he left behind, all text.

The CNA monograph is a free PDF.
